title: High-Throughput TimescaleDB / Hypertable Architecture vs Native Partitioning
realWorldScenario: Your analytics ingestion pipeline processes 250,000 metrics per second into PostgreSQL. Native declarative partitioning by day creates 365 tables per year, but query planning overhead degrades, and compression is non-existent. The team evaluates TimescaleDB hypertables.
questionStatement: Compare PostgreSQL native declarative partitioning with TimescaleDB hypertables for high-throughput time-series data. Evaluate automatic chunk creation, native columnar compression (hybrid row/column storage), continuous aggregates, and data retention policies.
expectedConcepts: Automatic chunk creation fitting working set in shared_buffers
Incremental Continuous Aggregates combining raw and rolled-up data
hints: What happens to native partition planning when you have 1,000 partitions?
How does columnar compression reduce disk space for time-series floats and timestamps?
Continuous aggregates do not require full refreshes.
